description:
You are a DevOps engineer tasked with quickly debugging application logs. You have a log file located at /home/user/app/logs/app.log. Your goal is to extract all unique IP addresses that have triggered an ERROR in the logs. Each error log line includes the text ERROR followed by any number of characters, and then an IP address in the standard IPv4 format (e.g., 10.0.0.1). Write a single shell command that extracts the unique IPv4 addresses from all lines containing ERROR (case-sensitive) in /home/user/app/logs/app.log. Save the sorted, unique list of these IP addresses into a file named /home/user/app/logs/error_ips.txt. Each IP address should appear on its own line in ascending order. Example log line format for reference (do not hardcode these values, always extract IPs programmatically):
[2024-05-01 12:05:21] ERROR: connection failed from 10.0.0.1.
truth:
Pre-task setup:
- The directory /home/user/app/logs/ exists and is writable by the user.
- The file /home/user/app/logs/app.log exists with the following contents:
[2024-05-01 12:05:21] ERROR: connection failed from 10.0.0.1
[2024-05-01 12:10:00] INFO: user login from 192.168.1.10
[2024-05-01 12:12:35] ERROR: timeout from 172.16.0.5
[2024-05-01 12:12:37] ERROR: DROP from 192.168.1.10
[2024-05-01 12:13:01] WARN: attempt from 172.16.0.5
[2024-05-01 12:13:10] ERROR: failed auth from 10.0.0.2

Expected output:
- A file /home/user/app/logs/error_ips.txt is created with the following content (sorted, unique, no trailing whitespace):

10.0.0.1
10.0.0.2
172.16.0.5
192.168.1.10

(No blank lines before or after, each line is only an IP address matched from an ERROR line.)

Permissions:
- The user has read and write access to /home/user/app/logs/app.log and can create files in /home/user/app/logs/.

No other files or changes are expected.
